name: GraphML XML graph deserialization
description:
boost::read_graphml parses an untrusted GraphML (XML) document from a std::istream into a BGL graph object, driving an internal property-tree based XML parser and then walking the resulting tree to create vertices/edges and set dynamic (runtime-typed) properties on them; this is a classic "parse attacker-controlled structured text into in-memory objects" surface where XML well-formedness, malformed/missing attributes, type-confused "attr.type" values, and structural graph constraints (directed vs undirected edges, duplicate/parallel edges, nested "graph" elements/"desired_idx" selection) must all be handled without memory corruption or uncaught exceptions escaping as crashes. The entry template wraps the attacker's MutableGraph/dynamic_properties pair in a mutate_graph_impl adaptor and calls the non-template boost::read_graphml(istream&, mutate_graph&, size_t), whose graphml_reader::run() first invokes boost::property_tree::read_xml() (no_comments | trim_whitespace) to build a ptree from the raw bytes, then walks the ptree: it collects <key> definitions (id/for/attr.name/attr.type/default), recursively finds <graph> elements (honoring desired_idx or -1 for "all"), then for each selected graph adds <node> elements as vertices (handle_vertex), applies default node properties, then processes <edge> elements (handle_edge), checking the edge's "directed" attribute against the graph's actual directedness (throwing directed_graph_error/undirected_graph_error on mismatch) and against parallel-edge constraints (bad_parallel_edge), and finally dispatches each <data> element's string value, through mutate_graph_impl::set_graph_property/set_vertex_property/set_edge_property, which use mpl::for_each over {bool,int,long,float,double,string} and boost::lexical_cast to convert the raw string according to the attr.type text, throwing parse_error on bad_lexical_cast or unknown type names.
- read_graphml(istream&, MutableGraph&, dynamic_properties&, desired_idx): target; builds mutate_graph_impl and calls core graphml_reader::run.
- read_graphml(istream&, mutate_graph&, desired_idx): the non-template overload actually implementing the core; same core, it is what the template entry calls, so using it directly is an equivalent/alternative entry but still exercises all of the core.
- write_graphml(ostream&, Graph&, dynamic_properties&, bool ordered_vertices) [and the VertexIndexMap overload]: consumer / round-trip inverse; serializes the graph + dynamic_properties built by read_graphml back to GraphML XML, exercising the dp.get_string()/type-lookup machinery on the result and giving a read->write->(re-read) round trip that stresses more of the encode/decode logic together.
- dynamic_properties::property(name, PropertyMap): configuration; called before read_graphml to register which named GraphML keys map to which typed property maps (vertex_color_t, edge_weight_t, graph-level ref_property_map, etc.) — the set and types of registered properties change which branches of put_property/set_*_property (and thus which lexical_cast<T> instantiations) are exercised while parsing <data> elements.
Input space to fuzz (XML text fed through the istream, plus which properties are pre-registered on dynamic_properties before calling read_graphml):
  - desired_idx: 0 (first graph, most common), a specific index selecting one nested <graph>, or (size_t)-1 to process *all* graphs — the most permissive setting, running get_graphs recursively over every nested graph and exercising the most of handle_vertex/handle_edge/property dispatch.
  - <key> elements' for="..." attribute: graph | node | edge | hyperedge | port | endpoint | all | graphml (anything else throws parse_error) — selects which key_kind a given id is tagged with and therefore whether its default value feeds handle_graph_property/handle_node_property/handle_edge_property.
  - <key> attr.type: boolean | int | long | float | double | string (anything else triggers the "unrecognized type" parse_error path) — selects the lexical_cast<T> instantiation used in put_property for every <data> referencing that key, each a distinct parse path (and a source of bad_lexical_cast on malformed text, e.g. non-numeric string for int/float/double).
  - presence/absence of a <key>'s <default> child — toggles whether handle_vertex/handle_edge pre-seeds default-valued properties on every newly created vertex/edge (extra code path beyond processing explicit <data>).
  - <graph edgedefault="directed|undirected"> combined with a per-<edge directed="true|false|''"> override, compared against the MutableGraph's actual is_directed(): mismatches throw directed_graph_error / undirected_graph_error, exercising distinct error paths.
  - duplicate edges on a graph type that disallows parallel edges: triggers do_add_edge returning added=false and bad_parallel_edge being thrown.
  - nested/sibling <graph> structure (graphs inside node "data"? no — graphs nested as children of a <graph>) and multiple <key>/<node>/<edge>/<data> repetitions, malformed/missing required attributes (id, source, target, key) which make ptree::get<std::string> throw property_tree parse errors — these exercise the XML/ptree error handling boundary that a fuzzer is most likely to hit directly from raw bytes.
This list is incomplete; what the project's own fuzzers and tests (graphml_test.cpp) do with the target stays.
